excerpt_i18n.en: "Are cloud giants about to start doing heavy lifting again?" Recently, Amazon Web Services (AWS) invested $1 billion to form an "AI Resident Engineer" team. This seemingly backward-looking heavy-asset move has stirred considerable controversy in the tech circle. For a long time, international cloud giants have favored the story of "extreme standardization": opening up public cloud API interfaces and then earning easy money. As for heavy-duty on-site presence? Basically none. But in 2026, this model of selling standardized products while resting on one's laurels might be about to change. AWS is spending $1 billion to build a team of thousands of "embedded AI engineers," also known as FDEs (Field Deployment Engineers), who will directly station in client offices to help enterprises deploy Agents and build AI production systems hands-on. This is not an isolated case. Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and other AI and cloud giants have been heavily hiring FDE positions or setting up dedicated companies in the past six months, with total investments exceeding tens of billions of RMB. Domestically, Alibaba, ByteDance, Tencent, and other major model and cloud giants have also rapidly formed "on-site iron troops" in the first half of this year. "Deep on-site presence," "high-level outsourcing," "IT construction teams"... these slightly negative and outdated labels are now reappearing in the narratives of AI and cloud giants. Why have the cloud giants, once eager to earn money effortlessly, suddenly become keen on on-site customer service in the AGI era? Will they repeat the mistakes of domestic cloud giants?
excerpt_i18n.es: ¿Los gigantes de la nube volverán a meterse en faenas pesadas? Recientemente, Amazon Web Services (AWS) ha invertido 1.000 millones de dólares para crear un equipo de "ingenieros de IA in situ". Este movimiento de activos intensos, que parece un retroceso histórico, ha generado controversia en el sector tecnológico. Hay que saber que, durante mucho tiempo, los grandes actores internacionales de la nube han preferido contar la historia de la "estandarización extrema": abrir las API de la nube pública y luego tumbarse a contar dinero. ¿Ingenieros pesados in situ? Básicamente no los había. Pero hoy, en 2026, ese modelo de vender productos estandarizados sin esfuerzo podría cambiar. AWS está gastando 1.000 millones de dólares para formar un equipo de miles de "ingenieros de IA integrados".

excerpt_i18n.en:
Changing narratives, shifting allegiances—two recent executive moves at OpenAI are exposing its new calculations. According to leaks on social platform X, OpenAI security veteran and chief futurist Joshua Achiam recently announced his departure; almost simultaneously, Dean Ball, a Washington insider with deep White House political and business connections who helped draft U.S. national AI policy, joined OpenAI as "Head of Strategic Foresight." This one-out, one-in is far from a simple job swap. Many industry observers believe this signals that the idealistic technical safety faction, whose mission is "to ensure that AGI benefits all of humanity," is being marginalized within OpenAI, while "political-business operators" who understand policy-making and gamesmanship are entering the core of power. OpenAI's strategic narrative and arbitrage anchor are shifting.

01 The departing technical idealist: Who is Joshua Achiam? Joshua Achiam is widely regarded in the industry as a quintessential academic idealist. He earned dual bachelor's degrees in physics and aerospace engineering from the University of Florida, then pursued graduate studies at UC Berkeley—the global mecca of computing—where he obtained a Ph.D. in electrical engineering and computer science. In 2017, at age 25, Achiam entered OpenAI as an intern. At that time, OpenAI was still a pure, non-profit organization.
excerpt_i18n.es: Cambio de historia, cambio de apoyo. Dos recientes movimientos directivos están revelando los nuevos cálculos de OpenAI. Según una filtración en la plataforma social X, Joshua Achiam, veterano de seguridad de OpenAI y científico jefe de futuro, ha anunciado su renuncia. Casi al mismo tiempo, Dean Ball, un élite de Washington con profundos vínculos políticos y empresariales en la Casa Blanca y que participó en la redacción de la política nacional de IA de EE. UU., se ha unido a OpenAI como «responsable de futuro estratégico». Esta «salida y entrada» no es un simple cambio de puesto. Muchos observadores del sector consideran que este movimiento significa que la facción técnica idealista y de seguridad, cuya misión es «garantizar que la AGI beneficie a toda la humanidad», está siendo marginada.

items.title: 苹果 Vision Pro 副总裁 Paul Meade 跳槽 OpenAI
items.raw_excerpt: 据彭博社报道，苹果公司负责 Vision Pro 团队的副总裁保罗·米德（Paul Meade）即将离职，加入 OpenAI 的硬件团队。此举与苹果新 CEO 上任后进行人事调整、导致保罗·米德“变相降级”有关。 随着约翰·特努斯（John Ternus）接替库克出任苹果下一任 CEO，原芯片业务掌门人约翰尼·斯鲁吉（Johny Srouji）被提拔为首席硬件官。 斯鲁吉上任后对硬件工程部门进行了颇具争议的激进重组：保罗·米德以及其他几位硬件副总裁，被要求向新任硬件工程副总裁汤姆·马里布（Tom Marieb）汇报，而马里布再向斯鲁吉汇报。 这种管理层级的增加，让保罗·米德等高管感觉自己被“变相降级”，从而引发了离职。 据了解，保罗·米德在苹果工作了超过 15 年，早期负责过 iPad 和 iPhone 的项目管理。自 2017 年起他就加入了 Vision Products Group，并在过去 7 年中深度主导了 Vision Pro 的硬件工程开发。 在离职前，他正带领团队秘密研发苹果对标 Meta Ray-Ban 的第一款无显示屏智能眼镜，该产品原计划于 2027 年底发布。 米德离职后，其原职位将由其长期副手、现任 Vision Pro 和智能眼镜产品设计负责人弗莱彻·罗斯科普夫（Fletcher Rothkopf）接任。 OpenAI 为何招募米德？业内普遍认为，这背后是 OpenAI 硬件战略正从“设计概念”走向“工业制造”。 一年前，OpenAI 已经以 65 亿美元的巨额交易收购了由苹果前首席设计官乔尼·艾夫（Jony Ive）等人创立的 AI 硬件初创公司 io。 相比于乔尼·艾夫团队更偏向外观设计与产品哲学的风格，保罗·米德的加入为 OpenAI 带来了最缺乏的硬核工程能力——如何把极其复杂的传感器、低延迟架构、空间计算组件塞进一个紧凑的消费级设备里。

excerpt_i18n.en: According to Bloomberg, Apple Vice President Paul Meade, who led the Vision Pro team, is leaving to join OpenAI's hardware team. This move is related to a "de facto demotion" following personnel adjustments under Apple's new CEO. After John Ternus succeeded Tim Cook as Apple's next CEO, former chip chief Johny Srouji was promoted to Chief Hardware Officer. Srouji initiated a controversial and aggressive restructuring of the hardware engineering department: Paul Meade and several other hardware VPs were required to report to new Hardware Engineering VP Tom Marieb, who in turn reports to Srouji. This increase in management layers led Meade and other executives to feel they had been "de facto demoted," prompting their departures.
